land.text: the New Hampshire Grants, claimed by both New Hampshire and New York

predecessors.note: The USA dossier records the loss in 1777; the page: 'New Hampshire and New York had conflicting property claims over the land'.

land.text: Vermont's last shape, admitted to the Union on 4 March 1791

successors.note: New York consented on 6 March 1790 and the commissioners concluded the talks on 7 October 1790 with Vermont agreeing to pay New York '$30,000'.

capitals.name: Windsor
capitals.note: Infobox 'Windsor (1777-1784)'; the constitution was drafted at Elijah West's Windsor Tavern in 1777.

capitals.name: Castleton
capitals.note: Infobox 'Castleton (1784-1791)'; Bennington is not listed as a capital (the 1791 convention met there).

correction.text: the same outline as Cliopatria's 1783 shape, applied from 1777: the shape is unchanged, only the years are extended back

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Vermont starts in 1783 but the Republic was declared on 15 January 1777 as 'the Republic of New Connecticut' and renamed Vermont on 2 June 1777. The 1781-82 'East Union' and 'West Union' claims are drawn as a contested strip in the ledger, not as territory ('never formally annexed').

28,159 km2 (1783-1787). The page gives no area; the gazetteer shows the shape covers 87% of present Vermont and spills 3% into New York and 5% into Massachusetts at the cell edge, so it is the Vermont of the Grants within grid precision. Nothing on the page moves the border in 1783-1790.

Same outline as 1783-1787. The Cliopatria row ends in 1790 but Vermont was admitted on 4 March 1791, which is when the dossier ends; the March 1790 and October 1790 New York settlement removed the rival claim without changing the land.

region.text: the New Hampshire Grants between the Connecticut River and Lake Champlain (Cliopatria's Vermont shape)

ledger.note: 15 January 1777: Vermont declares independence as the Republic of New Connecticut. The page's infobox gives 'Independence: January 15, 1777'; the land is 'the New Hampshire Grants' claimed by New Hampshire and New York.
2 June 1777: the Republic of New Connecticut is renamed Vermont. The name was 'officially changed to Vermont' on June 2, 1777.

region.text: the adjacent New Hampshire towns east of the Connecticut River ('East Union') and New York towns on the other side of Vermont ('West Union'; Congress spoke of claims 'west of Lake Champlain') that Vermont claimed in 1781; approximate one-cell strip along Vermont's frontier

ledger.note: 1781: Vermont claims the 'East Union' and 'West Union'. In 1781 Vermont briefly claimed adjacent New Hampshire and New York townships (the page's wording, as read); on 20 August 1781 the Confederation Congress said it 'would not consider admitting that state to the Union' unless Vermont gave up its claims east of the Connecticut River and west of Lake Champlain. The page gives no township list, so the strip is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the adjacent New Hampshire towns east of the Connecticut River ('East Union') and New York towns on the other side of Vermont ('West Union'; Congress spoke of claims 'west of Lake Champlain') that Vermont claimed in 1781; approximate one-cell strip along Vermont's frontier

ledger.note: 1782: Vermont rescinds the claims. The unions were never formally annexed and Vermont rescinded the claims in 1782 (the page's wording, as read).

region.text: Vermont's territory, admitted to the Union

ledger.note: 4 March 1791: Vermont joins the United States. The Union admitted Vermont on March 4, 1791 (infobox '1 Stat. 191'), after a convention voted 105 to 2 on 10 January 1791 to apply and New York consented on 6 March 1790 for '$30,000'.

wars.name: New Hampshire Grants dispute
wars.outcome: Settled without a territorial change: New York's legislature consented to Vermont's statehood on 6 March 1790 and the commissioners concluded the talks on 7 October 1790, Vermont paying '$30,000'; Vermont entered the Union on 4 March 1791.
wars.note: A dispute of claims between Vermont, New York and New Hampshire; the page describes no campaign, so no contest zone is written for the Grants themselves.

wars.name: Haldimand negotiations
wars.outcome: No change: after the 1780 Royalton raid, Ethan Allen led secret talks with Frederick Haldimand about returning Vermont to British rule; 'The British accepted the republic's reunion terms', and Vermont ended the talks after Yorktown (1781).
wars.note: Not a war; listed because it threatened Vermont's allegiance.

certainty.note: The frontiers of the Grants were claims of New Hampshire and New York until the 1790 settlement; the Connecticut River on the east is the firmest line. The 1781 unions are the softest edge.

sources.title: Vermont Republic
sources.note: Independence 15 Jan 1777 as New Connecticut, renamed Vermont 2 June 1777, capitals, governors, the New York settlement of 1790, the 1781 Unions, Haldimand talks, admission 4 March 1791. The infobox area is not on the page as fetched.

notes:
Cliopatria's two Vermont shapes (1783-1787, 1788-1790) are the same 28,159 km2 outline. The page does not give an infobox area, so the area check was made against the gazetteer only (87% of present Vermont, 3% of New York and 5% of Massachusetts at the cell edge). Cliopatria starts the row in 1783 and ends it in 1790; the Republic ran 15 January 1777 to 4 March 1791, so this dossier adds a 1777-1782 keyframe (same outline) and ends in 1791.

One page opened (budget 1-2). Not on it: the day of the 1777 constitution, the townships of the 1781 unions, any fighting between Vermont and New York. A gap-filler could open 'New Hampshire Grants' and 'Haldimand affair'. The Eastern and Western Unions are drawn as a one-cell band along the frontier because the page names no towns.

Counterparts: united-states-of-america (am-07-c; its ledger has the 1777 loss to Vermont and the 4 March 1791 gain). New York and New Hampshire are US states without dossiers of their own.
